mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months in at least 5 out of the last 10 tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.03 mean excess return) when UNRATE is below 4% for two consecutive months in at least 6 out of the last 10 instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.04 mean excess return) during periods when GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters in at least 4 out of the last 8 episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.06 mean excess return) when INDPRO declines for three consecutive months in at least 3 out of the last 6 episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive months in at least 4 out of the last 8 episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 persons in a single month, combined with a concurrent decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a strong labor market expansion that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 increase AND UNRATE falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 mean excess return) when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE falls in the same month in at least 5 out of the last 10 instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is held constant for four consecutive months after a prior tightening cycle, market expectations of prolonged low rates increase, boosting equity valuations through lower discount rates and higher P/E multiples, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS unchanged for 4 consecutive months after a tightening cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.04 mean excess return) when FEDFUNDS is unchanged for four consecutive months after a tightening cycle in at least 3 out of the last 6 episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month increase in personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising while PAYEMS is flat) signals a precautionary buildup in household savings, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises while PAYEMS is flat in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.03 mean excess return) when RSAFS rises and PAYEMS is flat in the same month in at least 4 out of the last 8 episodes.
